Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Region is the Nunukan Regency Region.
2. Regional Government is the Regional Government of Nunukan Regency. 3. Regent is the Regent of Nunukan.
4. Regional Work Unit, hereinafter abbreviated as SKPD, is an auxiliary element of the Regent and DPRD in the implementation of Government Affairs which are the authority of the Region.
5. Technical Regional Work Unit, hereinafter referred to as technical SKPD, is a Regional Work Unit whose scope of duties and responsibilities includes matters of Women's Empowerment and/or Child Protection.
6. Child is a person who is not yet 18 (eighteen) years old, including a child still in the womb.
7. Woman is a human being of female sex and a person recognized by law as a woman.
8. Women's Empowerment is every effort to improve physical, mental spiritual, social capabilities, knowledge, and skills so that women are ready to be utilized according to their respective capabilities.
9. Fulfillment of Children's Rights is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights to live, grow, develop and participate, optimally in accordance with human dignity and worth and receive protection from violence and discrimination.
10. Violence is any act that results in misery or suffering either physically, sexually, psychologically, and/or domestic neglect including threats to commit acts, coercion, or unlawful deprivation of a person's freedom.
11. Victim is a woman and/or child who experiences misery and/or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence that occurs in the Nunukan Regency area.
12. Protection is all actions of prevention, services and empowerment to protect and guarantee the rights of women and children from acts of violence.
13. Prevention is an activity carried out to prevent the occurrence of acts of violence against women and children. 14. Service is an action taken as soon as possible to victims when seeing, hearing and knowing that violence against victims will occur, is occurring or has occurred.
15. Empowerment is the strengthening of women victims of violence to be able to endeavor and work independently after they are recovered and provided with health and social rehabilitation services.
16. Health Rehabilitation is an effort to restore the condition of victims including physical, psychological and social health so that victims can carry out their roles properly and normally both in the family and in society.
17. Social rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring and developing the ability of a person experiencing social dysfunction to be able to carry out their social functions normally.
18. Repatriation is an effort to return victims of violence from the regional area to their area of origin.
19. Social reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, substitute family or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims.
20. Integrated Service Center, hereinafter abbreviated as PPT, is a unit that provides integrated services for victims of violence and is integrated with PPT that provides integrated services for witnesses and/or victims of human trafficking crimes.

Article 11

(1) To implement Women's Empowerment as referred to in Article 6, the Regional Government organizes gender mainstreaming including: a establishing the implementation of gender mainstreaming; b coordinating, facilitating, and mediating gender mainstreaming; c facilitating institutional strengthening and development of gender mainstreaming mechanisms in government institutions, women's study centers, research and development institutions, non-governmental institutions; d implementing gender mainstreaming related to the fields of development, education, health, economy, law, Human Rights and politics, environment and socio-culture; e improving the quality of life of women related to the fields of development, education, health, economy, law, Human Rights and politics, environment and socio-culture; f integrating efforts to improve the quality of life of women related to the fields of development, education, health, economy, law, Human Rights and politics, environment and socio-culture; g coordinating the implementation of improving the quality of life of women related to the fields of development, education, health, economy, law, Human Rights and politics, environment and socio-culture; h organizing the protection of women especially protection for victims of violence, female workers, elderly women, and women with disabilities, in conflict areas and disaster-affected areas; i facilitating the integration of protection of women especially protection for victims of violence, female workers, elderly women and women with disabilities, in conflict areas and disaster-affected areas; j coordinating the protection of women especially protection for victims of violence, female workers, elderly women and women with disabilities; k facilitating the strengthening and development of networks of community institutions or organizations and the business world for the implementation of gender mainstreaming; l developing gender-based information systems; and m providing and organizing integrated or non-integrated services for women victims of violence, female workers, elderly women, and women with disabilities.

(2) Further provisions regarding the forms of women's empowerment and gender mainstreaming mechanisms as referred to in paragraph (1) are regulated by Regent Regulation.

Article 33

Other violence as referred to in Article 27 letter f is caused by:

a. threat of violence includes: any unlawful act in the form of speech, writing, images, symbols, or body movements, whether with or without the use of means that create fear or restrict a person's fundamental freedom; and
b. coercion, includes: a situation where a person/victim is ordered to do something in such a way that the person does something that is contrary to their own will.

Article 16

(1) Implementation of Fulfillment of Children's Rights in the field of health as referred to in Article 13 letter b, the Regional Government must provide facilities and organize comprehensive health services for children, so that every child obtains optimal health status from the womb, carried out gradually adjusted to regional financial capacity and supported by community participation.

(2) Comprehensive health services as referred to in paragraph (1) include: a promotional, preventive, curative and rehabilitative efforts for basic health services; b exemption from cost burden for malnourished children, children undergoing dialysis due to kidney failure, children with thalassemia major, children with disabilities, children with special needs, street children, children infected with HIV/AIDS, child workers, child victims of narcotics, alcohol, psychotropic and other addictive substances (NAPZA) abuse, children who become victims of violence, such as neglect, economically and sexually exploited and victims of human trafficking.

(3) Children as referred to in paragraph (2) are children from poor families except as otherwise regulated in accordance with health financing programs established by the government.

Article 54

(1) In the implementation of Protection of Women and children, the community can:

a. form family partners at the Kelurahan/Village level by the community;
b. conduct socialization of women's and children's rights independently; c. provide first aid to victims; and
d. report to the competent authorities if violence against victims occurs in their environment.
(2) Community participation as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out by individuals, community organizations, non-governmental organizations, educational institutions, religious institutions, private sector and/or mass media.

Article 50

(1) To ensure synergy, balance and effectiveness of integrated measures in the implementation of policies, programs, activities, protection of Women and children, the Government conducts monitoring.

(2) Monitoring as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out by the Technical SKPD and PPT.

(3) Monitoring as referred to in paragraph (1) is to determine the progress and obstacles in the implementation of policies, programs and activities for the Protection of Women and children.

(4) Monitoring is carried out periodically through coordination and direct monitoring of SKPDs that implement policies, activities for the protection of Women and children victims of violence.

(5) Monitoring is carried out from planning to implementation of policies, programs and activities for the protection of women and children every year.

Article 4

Every Woman has the right: a to life and the right to maintain life and livelihood; b to form a family and continue descendants through lawful marriage; c to develop themselves through the fulfillment of their basic needs; d to receive education and benefit from science and technology, arts and culture, in order to improve the quality of life and for the welfare of humanity; e to advance themselves in fighting for their rights collectively to build society, nation and state; f to recognition, guarantee, protection and fair legal certainty as well as equal treatment before the law; g to work and receive fair and proper remuneration and treatment in employment relations; h to obtain equal opportunities in government; i to freedom of association, assembly and expression of opinion; j to protection of personal self, family, honor, dignity and

| property under their control, and the right to a sense of | security and protection from the threat of fear to do | or not do something that is a fundamental right; |
|---|---|---|
| k to be free from torture or treatment that degrades | human dignity and the right to obtain political asylum | from other countries; |
| l to live prosperously physically and spiritually, to reside and receive | a good and healthy living environment, and the right to obtain | health services; |

m to social security that enables their full development as dignified human beings; n to equality of position in law and government; o to work and a decent livelihood for humanity; p in the effort to defend the state; q to communicate and obtain information to develop their personal and social environment, and the right to seek, obtain, possess, store, process, and convey information using all types of available channels; r to embrace their respective religions and to worship according to their religion and beliefs; and s to receive education.

19. Social reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, substitute family or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims.

Article 33

Other violence as referred to in Article 27 letter f is caused by:

a. threat of violence includes: any unlawful act in the form of speech, writing, images, symbols, or body movements, whether with or without the use of means that create fear or restrict a person's fundamental freedom; and

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Region is the Nunukan Regency Region.
2. Regional Government is the Regional Government of Nunukan Regency. 3. Regent is the Regent of Nunukan.
4. Regional Work Unit, hereinafter abbreviated as SKPD, is an auxiliary element of the Regent and DPRD in the implementation of Government Affairs which are the authority of the Region.
5. Technical Regional Work Unit, hereinafter referred to as technical SKPD, is a Regional Work Unit whose scope of duties and responsibilities includes matters of Women's Empowerment and/or Child Protection.
6. Child is a person who is not yet 18 (eighteen) years old, including a child still in the womb.
7. Woman is a human being of female sex and a person recognized by law as a woman.
8. Women's Empowerment is every effort to improve physical, mental spiritual, social capabilities, knowledge, and skills so that women are ready to be utilized according to their respective capabilities.
9. Fulfillment of Children's Rights is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights to live, grow, develop and participate, optimally in accordance with human dignity and worth and receive protection from violence and discrimination.
10. Violence is any act that results in misery or suffering either physically, sexually, psychologically, and/or domestic neglect including threats to commit acts, coercion, or unlawful deprivation of a person's freedom.
11. Victim is a woman and/or child who experiences misery and/or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence that occurs in the Nunukan Regency area.
12. Protection is all actions of prevention, services and empowerment to protect and guarantee the rights of women and children from acts of violence.
13. Prevention is an activity carried out to prevent the occurrence of acts of violence against women and children. 14. Service is an action taken as soon as possible to victims when seeing, hearing and knowing that violence against victims will occur, is occurring or has occurred.
15. Empowerment is the strengthening of women victims of violence to be able to endeavor and work independently after they are recovered and provided with health and social rehabilitation services.
16. Health Rehabilitation is an effort to restore the condition of victims including physical, psychological and social health so that victims can carry out their roles properly and normally both in the family and in society.
17. Social rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring and developing the ability of a person experiencing social dysfunction to be able to carry out their social functions normally.
18. Repatriation is an effort to return victims of violence from the regional area to their area of origin.
19. Social reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, substitute family or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims.
20. Integrated Service Center, hereinafter abbreviated as PPT, is a unit that provides integrated services for victims of violence and is integrated with PPT that provides integrated services for witnesses and/or victims of human trafficking crimes.

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Region is the Nunukan Regency Region.
2. Regional Government is the Regional Government of Nunukan Regency. 3. Regent is the Regent of Nunukan.
4. Regional Work Unit, hereinafter abbreviated as SKPD, is an auxiliary element of the Regent and DPRD in the implementation of Government Affairs which are the authority of the Region.
5. Technical Regional Work Unit, hereinafter referred to as technical SKPD, is a Regional Work Unit whose scope of duties and responsibilities includes matters of Women's Empowerment and/or Child Protection.
6. Child is a person who is not yet 18 (eighteen) years old, including a child still in the womb.
7. Woman is a human being of female sex and a person recognized by law as a woman.
8. Women's Empowerment is every effort to improve physical, mental spiritual, social capabilities, knowledge, and skills so that women are ready to be utilized according to their respective capabilities.
9. Fulfillment of Children's Rights is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights to live, grow, develop and participate, optimally in accordance with human dignity and worth and receive protection from violence and discrimination.
10. Violence is any act that results in misery or suffering either physically, sexually, psychologically, and/or domestic neglect including threats to commit acts, coercion, or unlawful deprivation of a person's freedom.
11. Victim is a woman and/or child who experiences misery and/or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence that occurs in the Nunukan Regency area.
12. Protection is all actions of prevention, services and empowerment to protect and guarantee the rights of women and children from acts of violence.
13. Prevention is an activity carried out to prevent the occurrence of acts of violence against women and children. 14. Service is an action taken as soon as possible to victims when seeing, hearing and knowing that violence against victims will occur, is occurring or has occurred.
15. Empowerment is the strengthening of women victims of violence to be able to endeavor and work independently after they are recovered and provided with health and social rehabilitation services.
16. Health Rehabilitation is an effort to restore the condition of victims including physical, psychological and social health so that victims can carry out their roles properly and normally both in the family and in society.
17. Social rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring and developing the ability of a person experiencing social dysfunction to be able to carry out their social functions normally.
18. Repatriation is an effort to return victims of violence from the regional area to their area of origin.

c. any form of exploitation of sexual organs or other organs of the victim to obtain benefits, including but not limited to all activities of prostitution or obscenity.

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Region is the Nunukan Regency Region.
2. Regional Government is the Regional Government of Nunukan Regency. 3. Regent is the Regent of Nunukan.
4. Regional Work Unit, hereinafter abbreviated as SKPD, is an auxiliary element of the Regent and DPRD in the implementation of Government Affairs which are the authority of the Region.
5. Technical Regional Work Unit, hereinafter referred to as technical SKPD, is a Regional Work Unit whose scope of duties and responsibilities includes matters of Women's Empowerment and/or Child Protection.
6. Child is a person who is not yet 18 (eighteen) years old, including a child still in the womb.
7. Woman is a human being of female sex and a person recognized by law as a woman.
8. Women's Empowerment is every effort to improve physical, mental spiritual, social capabilities, knowledge, and skills so that women are ready to be utilized according to their respective capabilities.
9. Fulfillment of Children's Rights is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights to live, grow, develop and participate, optimally in accordance with human dignity and worth and receive protection from violence and discrimination.
10. Violence is any act that results in misery or suffering either physically, sexually, psychologically, and/or domestic neglect including threats to commit acts, coercion, or unlawful deprivation of a person's freedom.
11. Victim is a woman and/or child who experiences misery and/or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence that occurs in the Nunukan Regency area.
12. Protection is all actions of prevention, services and empowerment to protect and guarantee the rights of women and children from acts of violence.
13. Prevention is an activity carried out to prevent the occurrence of acts of violence against women and children. 14. Service is an action taken as soon as possible to victims when seeing, hearing and knowing that violence against victims will occur, is occurring or has occurred.
15. Empowerment is the strengthening of women victims of violence to be able to endeavor and work independently after they are recovered and provided with health and social rehabilitation services.
16. Health Rehabilitation is an effort to restore the condition of victims including physical, psychological and social health so that victims can carry out their roles properly and normally both in the family and in society.
17. Social rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring and developing the ability of a person experiencing social dysfunction to be able to carry out their social functions normally.
18. Repatriation is an effort to return victims of violence from the regional area to their area of origin.
19. Social reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, substitute family or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims.
20. Integrated Service Center, hereinafter abbreviated as PPT, is a unit that provides integrated services for victims of violence and is integrated with PPT that provides integrated services for witnesses and/or victims of human trafficking crimes.

HAS DECIDED :

To Establish : REGIONAL REGULATION OF NUNUKAN REGENCY CONCERNING THE IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN.

CHAPTER II

PRINCIPLES AND OBJECTIVES

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Region is the Nunukan Regency Region.
2. Regional Government is the Regional Government of Nunukan Regency. 3. Regent is the Regent of Nunukan.
4. Regional Work Unit, hereinafter abbreviated as SKPD, is an auxiliary element of the Regent and DPRD in the implementation of Government Affairs which are the authority of the Region.
5. Technical Regional Work Unit, hereinafter referred to as technical SKPD, is a Regional Work Unit whose scope of duties and responsibilities includes matters of Women's Empowerment and/or Child Protection.
6. Child is a person who is not yet 18 (eighteen) years old, including a child still in the womb.
7. Woman is a human being of female sex and a person recognized by law as a woman.
8. Women's Empowerment is every effort to improve physical, mental spiritual, social capabilities, knowledge, and skills so that women are ready to be utilized according to their respective capabilities.
9. Fulfillment of Children's Rights is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights to live, grow, develop and participate, optimally in accordance with human dignity and worth and receive protection from violence and discrimination.
10. Violence is any act that results in misery or suffering either physically, sexually, psychologically, and/or domestic neglect including threats to commit acts, coercion, or unlawful deprivation of a person's freedom.
11. Victim is a woman and/or child who experiences misery and/or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence that occurs in the Nunukan Regency area.
12. Protection is all actions of prevention, services and empowerment to protect and guarantee the rights of women and children from acts of violence.
13. Prevention is an activity carried out to prevent the occurrence of acts of violence against women and children. 14. Service is an action taken as soon as possible to victims when seeing, hearing and knowing that violence against victims will occur, is occurring or has occurred.
15. Empowerment is the strengthening of women victims of violence to be able to endeavor and work independently after they are recovered and provided with health and social rehabilitation services.
16. Health Rehabilitation is an effort to restore the condition of victims including physical, psychological and social health so that victims can carry out their roles properly and normally both in the family and in society.
17. Social rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring and developing the ability of a person experiencing social dysfunction to be able to carry out their social functions normally.
18. Repatriation is an effort to return victims of violence from the regional area to their area of origin.
19. Social reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, substitute family or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims.
20. Integrated Service Center, hereinafter abbreviated as PPT, is a unit that provides integrated services for victims of violence and is integrated with PPT that provides integrated services for witnesses and/or victims of human trafficking crimes.

Article 50

(1) To ensure synergy, balance and effectiveness of integrated measures in the implementation of policies, programs, activities, protection of Women and children, the Government conducts monitoring.

(2) Monitoring as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out by the Technical SKPD and PPT.

(3) Monitoring as referred to in paragraph (1) is to determine the progress and obstacles in the implementation of policies, programs and activities for the Protection of Women and children.

Article 51

(1) Evaluation of the implementation of policies, programs and activities for the Protection of Women and children victims of violence is carried out at the end of each Fiscal year or when needed as required.

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Region is the Nunukan Regency Region.
2. Regional Government is the Regional Government of Nunukan Regency. 3. Regent is the Regent of Nunukan.
4. Regional Work Unit, hereinafter abbreviated as SKPD, is an auxiliary element of the Regent and DPRD in the implementation of Government Affairs which are the authority of the Region.
5. Technical Regional Work Unit, hereinafter referred to as technical SKPD, is a Regional Work Unit whose scope of duties and responsibilities includes matters of Women's Empowerment and/or Child Protection.
6. Child is a person who is not yet 18 (eighteen) years old, including a child still in the womb.
7. Woman is a human being of female sex and a person recognized by law as a woman.
8. Women's Empowerment is every effort to improve physical, mental spiritual, social capabilities, knowledge, and skills so that women are ready to be utilized according to their respective capabilities.
9. Fulfillment of Children's Rights is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights to live, grow, develop and participate, optimally in accordance with human dignity and worth and receive protection from violence and discrimination.
10. Violence is any act that results in misery or suffering either physically, sexually, psychologically, and/or domestic neglect including threats to commit acts, coercion, or unlawful deprivation of a person's freedom.
11. Victim is a woman and/or child who experiences misery and/or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence that occurs in the Nunukan Regency area.
12. Protection is all actions of prevention, services and empowerment to protect and guarantee the rights of women and children from acts of violence.
13. Prevention is an activity carried out to prevent the occurrence of acts of violence against women and children. 14. Service is an action taken as soon as possible to victims when seeing, hearing and knowing that violence against victims will occur, is occurring or has occurred.
15. Empowerment is the strengthening of women victims of violence to be able to endeavor and work independently after they are recovered and provided with health and social rehabilitation services.
16. Health Rehabilitation is an effort to restore the condition of victims including physical, psychological and social health so that victims can carry out their roles properly and normally both in the family and in society.
17. Social rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring and developing the ability of a person experiencing social dysfunction to be able to carry out their social functions normally.
18. Repatriation is an effort to return victims of violence from the regional area to their area of origin.
19. Social reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, substitute family or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims.
20. Integrated Service Center, hereinafter abbreviated as PPT, is a unit that provides integrated services for victims of violence and is integrated with PPT that provides integrated services for witnesses and/or victims of human trafficking crimes.

Article 18

(1) Implementation of Fulfillment of Children's Rights in the field of education as referred to in Article 13 letter c, the Regional Government guarantees the implementation of a 12 (twelve) year compulsory education program for all children.

(2) Every organizer of an education unit must provide opportunities for children to obtain educational services without discrimination.

Article 15

Implementation of Fulfillment of Children's Rights in the field of birth registration, as referred to in Article 13 letter a, the Regional Government is obliged to organize birth registration of children with the issuance of birth certificates in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

Article 50

(1) To ensure synergy, balance and effectiveness of integrated measures in the implementation of policies, programs, activities, protection of Women and children, the Government conducts monitoring.

(2) Monitoring as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out by the Technical SKPD and PPT.

(3) Monitoring as referred to in paragraph (1) is to determine the progress and obstacles in the implementation of policies, programs and activities for the Protection of Women and children.

(4) Monitoring is carried out periodically through coordination and direct monitoring of SKPDs that implement policies, activities for the protection of Women and children victims of violence.

(5) Monitoring is carried out from planning to implementation of policies, programs and activities for the protection of women and children every year.

3.1.text:
Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Region is the Nunukan Regency Region.
2. Regional Government is the Regional Government of Nunukan Regency. 3. Regent is the Regent of Nunukan.
4. Regional Work Unit, hereinafter abbreviated as SKPD, is an auxiliary element of the Regent and DPRD in the implementation of Government Affairs which are the authority of the Region.
5. Technical Regional Work Unit, hereinafter referred to as technical SKPD, is a Regional Work Unit whose scope of duties and responsibilities includes matters of Women's Empowerment and/or Child Protection.
6. Child is a person who is not yet 18 (eighteen) years old, including a child still in the womb.
7. Woman is a human being of female sex and a person recognized by law as a woman.
8. Women's Empowerment is every effort to improve physical, mental spiritual, social capabilities, knowledge, and skills so that women are ready to be utilized according to their respective capabilities.
9. Fulfillment of Children's Rights is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights to live, grow, develop and participate, optimally in accordance with human dignity and worth and receive protection from violence and discrimination.
10. Violence is any act that results in misery or suffering either physically, sexually, psychologically, and/or domestic neglect including threats to commit acts, coercion, or unlawful deprivation of a person's freedom.
11. Victim is a woman and/or child who experiences misery and/or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence that occurs in the Nunukan Regency area.
12. Protection is all actions of prevention, services and empowerment to protect and guarantee the rights of women and children from acts of violence.
13. Prevention is an activity carried out to prevent the occurrence of acts of violence against women and children. 14. Service is an action taken as soon as possible to victims when seeing, hearing and knowing that violence against victims will occur, is occurring or has occurred.
15. Empowerment is the strengthening of women victims of violence to be able to endeavor and work independently after they are recovered and provided with health and social rehabilitation services.
16. Health Rehabilitation is an effort to restore the condition of victims including physical, psychological and social health so that victims can carry out their roles properly and normally both in the family and in society.
17. Social rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring and developing the ability of a person experiencing social dysfunction to be able to carry out their social functions normally.
18. Repatriation is an effort to return victims of violence from the regional area to their area of origin.
19. Social reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, substitute family or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims.
20. Integrated Service Center, hereinafter abbreviated as PPT, is a unit that provides integrated services for victims of violence and is integrated with PPT that provides integrated services for witnesses and/or victims of human trafficking crimes.

Article 11

(1) To implement Women's Empowerment as referred to in Article 6, the Regional Government organizes gender mainstreaming including: a establishing the implementation of gender mainstreaming; b coordinating, facilitating, and mediating gender mainstreaming; c facilitating institutional strengthening and development of gender mainstreaming mechanisms in government institutions, women's study centers, research and development institutions, non-governmental institutions; d implementing gender mainstreaming related to the fields of development, education, health, economy, law, Human Rights and politics, environment and socio-culture; e improving the quality of life of women related to the fields of development, education, health, economy, law, Human Rights and politics, environment and socio-culture; f integrating efforts to improve the quality of life of women related to the fields of development, education, health, economy, law, Human Rights and politics, environment and socio-culture; g coordinating the implementation of improving the quality of life of women related to the fields of development, education, health, economy, law, Human Rights and politics, environment and socio-culture; h organizing the protection of women especially protection for victims of violence, female workers, elderly women, and women with disabilities, in conflict areas and disaster-affected areas; i facilitating the integration of protection of women especially protection for victims of violence, female workers, elderly women and women with disabilities, in conflict areas and disaster-affected areas; j coordinating the protection of women especially protection for victims of violence, female workers, elderly women and women with disabilities; k facilitating the strengthening and development of networks of community institutions or organizations and the business world for the implementation of gender mainstreaming; l developing gender-based information systems; and m providing and organizing integrated or non-integrated services for women victims of violence, female workers, elderly women, and women with disabilities.

(2) Further provisions regarding the forms of women's empowerment and gender mainstreaming mechanisms as referred to in paragraph (1) are regulated by Regent Regulation.

Article 50

(1) To ensure synergy, balance and effectiveness of integrated measures in the implementation of policies, programs, activities, protection of Women and children, the Government conducts monitoring.

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Region is the Nunukan Regency Region.

6. Child is a person who is not yet 18 (eighteen) years old, including a child still in the womb.
7. Woman is a human being of female sex and a person recognized by law as a woman.
8. Women's Empowerment is every effort to improve physical, mental spiritual, social capabilities, knowledge, and skills so that women are ready to be utilized according to their respective capabilities.

11. Victim is a woman and/or child who experiences misery and/or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence that occurs in the Nunukan Regency area.
12. Protection is all actions of prevention, services and empowerment to protect and guarantee the rights of women and children from acts of violence.

17. Social rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring and developing the ability of a person experiencing social dysfunction to be able to carry out their social functions normally.
18. Repatriation is an effort to return victims of violence from the regional area to their area of origin.
19. Social reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, substitute family or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims.
20. Integrated Service Center, hereinafter abbreviated as PPT, is a unit that provides integrated services for victims of violence and is integrated with PPT that provides integrated services for witnesses and/or victims of human trafficking crimes.

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Region is the Nunukan Regency Region.
2. Regional Government is the Regional Government of Nunukan Regency. 3. Regent is the Regent of Nunukan.
4. Regional Work Unit, hereinafter abbreviated as SKPD, is an auxiliary element of the Regent and DPRD in the implementation of Government Affairs which are the authority of the Region.
5. Technical Regional Work Unit, hereinafter referred to as technical SKPD, is a Regional Work Unit whose scope of duties and responsibilities includes matters of Women's Empowerment and/or Child Protection.
6. Child is a person who is not yet 18 (eighteen) years old, including a child still in the womb.
7. Woman is a human being of female sex and a person recognized by law as a woman.
8. Women's Empowerment is every effort to improve physical, mental spiritual, social capabilities, knowledge, and skills so that women are ready to be utilized according to their respective capabilities.
9. Fulfillment of Children's Rights is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights to live, grow, develop and participate, optimally in accordance with human dignity and worth and receive protection from violence and discrimination.
10. Violence is any act that results in misery or suffering either physically, sexually, psychologically, and/or domestic neglect including threats to commit acts, coercion, or unlawful deprivation of a person's freedom.
11. Victim is a woman and/or child who experiences misery and/or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence that occurs in the Nunukan Regency area.
12. Protection is all actions of prevention, services and empowerment to protect and guarantee the rights of women and children from acts of violence.
13. Prevention is an activity carried out to prevent the occurrence of acts of violence against women and children. 14. Service is an action taken as soon as possible to victims when seeing, hearing and knowing that violence against victims will occur, is occurring or has occurred.
15. Empowerment is the strengthening of women victims of violence to be able to endeavor and work independently after they are recovered and provided with health and social rehabilitation services.
16. Health Rehabilitation is an effort to restore the condition of victims including physical, psychological and social health so that victims can carry out their roles properly and normally both in the family and in society.
17. Social rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring and developing the ability of a person experiencing social dysfunction to be able to carry out their social functions normally.
18. Repatriation is an effort to return victims of violence from the regional area to their area of origin.
19. Social reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, substitute family or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims.
20. Integrated Service Center, hereinafter abbreviated as PPT, is a unit that provides integrated services for victims of violence and is integrated with PPT that provides integrated services for witnesses and/or victims of human trafficking crimes.

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Region is the Nunukan Regency Region.
2. Regional Government is the Regional Government of Nunukan Regency. 3. Regent is the Regent of Nunukan.
4. Regional Work Unit, hereinafter abbreviated as SKPD, is an auxiliary element of the Regent and DPRD in the implementation of Government Affairs which are the authority of the Region.
5. Technical Regional Work Unit, hereinafter referred to as technical SKPD, is a Regional Work Unit whose scope of duties and responsibilities includes matters of Women's Empowerment and/or Child Protection.
6. Child is a person who is not yet 18 (eighteen) years old, including a child still in the womb.
7. Woman is a human being of female sex and a person recognized by law as a woman.
8. Women's Empowerment is every effort to improve physical, mental spiritual, social capabilities, knowledge, and skills so that women are ready to be utilized according to their respective capabilities.
9. Fulfillment of Children's Rights is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights to live, grow, develop and participate, optimally in accordance with human dignity and worth and receive protection from violence and discrimination.
10. Violence is any act that results in misery or suffering either physically, sexually, psychologically, and/or domestic neglect including threats to commit acts, coercion, or unlawful deprivation of a person's freedom.
11. Victim is a woman and/or child who experiences misery and/or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence that occurs in the Nunukan Regency area.
12. Protection is all actions of prevention, services and empowerment to protect and guarantee the rights of women and children from acts of violence.
13. Prevention is an activity carried out to prevent the occurrence of acts of violence against women and children. 14. Service is an action taken as soon as possible to victims when seeing, hearing and knowing that violence against victims will occur, is occurring or has occurred.
15. Empowerment is the strengthening of women victims of violence to be able to endeavor and work independently after they are recovered and provided with health and social rehabilitation services.
16. Health Rehabilitation is an effort to restore the condition of victims including physical, psychological and social health so that victims can carry out their roles properly and normally both in the family and in society.
17. Social rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring and developing the ability of a person experiencing social dysfunction to be able to carry out their social functions normally.
18. Repatriation is an effort to return victims of violence from the regional area to their area of origin.
19. Social reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, substitute family or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims.
20. Integrated Service Center, hereinafter abbreviated as PPT, is a unit that provides integrated services for victims of violence and is integrated with PPT that provides integrated services for witnesses and/or victims of human trafficking crimes.

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Region is the Nunukan Regency Region.
2. Regional Government is the Regional Government of Nunukan Regency. 3. Regent is the Regent of Nunukan.
4. Regional Work Unit, hereinafter abbreviated as SKPD, is an auxiliary element of the Regent and DPRD in the implementation of Government Affairs which are the authority of the Region.
5. Technical Regional Work Unit, hereinafter referred to as technical SKPD, is a Regional Work Unit whose scope of duties and responsibilities includes matters of Women's Empowerment and/or Child Protection.
6. Child is a person who is not yet 18 (eighteen) years old, including a child still in the womb.
7. Woman is a human being of female sex and a person recognized by law as a woman.
8. Women's Empowerment is every effort to improve physical, mental spiritual, social capabilities, knowledge, and skills so that women are ready to be utilized according to their respective capabilities.
9. Fulfillment of Children's Rights is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights to live, grow, develop and participate, optimally in accordance with human dignity and worth and receive protection from violence and discrimination.
10. Violence is any act that results in misery or suffering either physically, sexually, psychologically, and/or domestic neglect including threats to commit acts, coercion, or unlawful deprivation of a person's freedom.
11. Victim is a woman and/or child who experiences misery and/or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence that occurs in the Nunukan Regency area.
12. Protection is all actions of prevention, services and empowerment to protect and guarantee the rights of women and children from acts of violence.
13. Prevention is an activity carried out to prevent the occurrence of acts of violence against women and children. 14. Service is an action taken as soon as possible to victims when seeing, hearing and knowing that violence against victims will occur, is occurring or has occurred.
15. Empowerment is the strengthening of women victims of violence to be able to endeavor and work independently after they are recovered and provided with health and social rehabilitation services.
16. Health Rehabilitation is an effort to restore the condition of victims including physical, psychological and social health so that victims can carry out their roles properly and normally both in the family and in society.
17. Social rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring and developing the ability of a person experiencing social dysfunction to be able to carry out their social functions normally.
18. Repatriation is an effort to return victims of violence from the regional area to their area of origin.
19. Social reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, substitute family or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims.
20. Integrated Service Center, hereinafter abbreviated as PPT, is a unit that provides integrated services for victims of violence and is integrated with PPT that provides integrated services for witnesses and/or victims of human trafficking crimes.

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Region is the Nunukan Regency Region.
2. Regional Government is the Regional Government of Nunukan Regency. 3. Regent is the Regent of Nunukan.
4. Regional Work Unit, hereinafter abbreviated as SKPD, is an auxiliary element of the Regent and DPRD in the implementation of Government Affairs which are the authority of the Region.
5. Technical Regional Work Unit, hereinafter referred to as technical SKPD, is a Regional Work Unit whose scope of duties and responsibilities includes matters of Women's Empowerment and/or Child Protection.
6. Child is a person who is not yet 18 (eighteen) years old, including a child still in the womb.
7. Woman is a human being of female sex and a person recognized by law as a woman.
8. Women's Empowerment is every effort to improve physical, mental spiritual, social capabilities, knowledge, and skills so that women are ready to be utilized according to their respective capabilities.
9. Fulfillment of Children's Rights is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights to live, grow, develop and participate, optimally in accordance with human dignity and worth and receive protection from violence and discrimination.
10. Violence is any act that results in misery or suffering either physically, sexually, psychologically, and/or domestic neglect including threats to commit acts, coercion, or unlawful deprivation of a person's freedom.
11. Victim is a woman and/or child who experiences misery and/or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence that occurs in the Nunukan Regency area.
12. Protection is all actions of prevention, services and empowerment to protect and guarantee the rights of women and children from acts of violence.
13. Prevention is an activity carried out to prevent the occurrence of acts of violence against women and children. 14. Service is an action taken as soon as possible to victims when seeing, hearing and knowing that violence against victims will occur, is occurring or has occurred.
15. Empowerment is the strengthening of women victims of violence to be able to endeavor and work independently after they are recovered and provided with health and social rehabilitation services.
16. Health Rehabilitation is an effort to restore the condition of victims including physical, psychological and social health so that victims can carry out their roles properly and normally both in the family and in society.
17. Social rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring and developing the ability of a person experiencing social dysfunction to be able to carry out their social functions normally.
18. Repatriation is an effort to return victims of violence from the regional area to their area of origin.
19. Social reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, substitute family or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims.
20. Integrated Service Center, hereinafter abbreviated as PPT, is a unit that provides integrated services for victims of violence and is integrated with PPT that provides integrated services for witnesses and/or victims of human trafficking crimes.

Article 51

(1) Evaluation of the implementation of policies, programs and activities for the Protection of Women and children victims of violence is carried out at the end of each Fiscal year or when needed as required.

(2) The results of the evaluation of the implementation of policies, programs and activities for the protection of Women and children victims of violence are used as input for the formulation of policies, programs and activities for the protection of Women and children victims of violence for the following year.

(3) Evaluation as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

Article 11

d implementing gender mainstreaming related to the fields of development, education, health, economy, law, Human Rights and politics, environment and socio-culture; e improving the quality of life of women related to the fields of development, education, health, economy, law, Human Rights and politics, environment and socio-culture; f integrating efforts to improve the quality of life of women related to the fields of development, education, health, economy, law, Human Rights and politics, environment and socio-culture; g coordinating the implementation of improving the quality of life of women related to the fields of development, education, health, economy, law, Human Rights and politics, environment and socio-culture; Article 50

Article 1

5. Technical Regional Work Unit, hereinafter referred to as technical SKPD, is a Regional Work Unit whose scope of duties and responsibilities includes matters of Women's Empowerment and/or Child Protection.
6. Child is a person who is not yet 18 (eighteen) years old, including a child still in the womb.
7. Woman is a human being of female sex and a person recognized by law as a woman.
8. Women's Empowerment is every effort to improve physical, mental spiritual, social capabilities, knowledge, and skills so that women are ready to be utilized according to their respective capabilities.
9. Fulfillment of Children's Rights is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights to live, grow, develop and participate, optimally in accordance with human dignity and worth and receive protection from violence and discrimination.
10. Violence is any act that results in misery or suffering either physically, sexually, psychologically, and/or domestic neglect including threats to commit acts, coercion, or unlawful deprivation of a person's freedom.
11. Victim is a woman and/or child who experiences misery and/or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence that occurs in the Nunukan Regency area.
12. Protection is all actions of prevention, services and empowerment to protect and guarantee the rights of women and children from acts of violence.
13. Prevention is an activity carried out to prevent the occurrence of acts of violence against women and children. 14. Service is an action taken as soon as possible to victims when seeing, hearing and knowing that violence against victims will occur, is occurring or has occurred.
15. Empowerment is the strengthening of women victims of violence to be able to endeavor and work independently after they are recovered and provided with health and social rehabilitation services.
16. Health Rehabilitation is an effort to restore the condition of victims including physical, psychological and social health so that victims can carry out their roles properly and normally both in the family and in society.
17. Social rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring and developing the ability of a person experiencing social dysfunction to be able to carry out their social functions normally.
18. Repatriation is an effort to return victims of violence from the regional area to their area of origin.
19. Social reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, substitute family or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims.
20. Integrated Service Center, hereinafter abbreviated as PPT, is a unit that provides integrated services for victims of violence and is integrated with PPT that provides integrated services for witnesses and/or victims of human trafficking crimes.

16. Health Rehabilitation is an effort to restore the condition of victims including physical, psychological and social health so that victims can carry out their roles properly and normally both in the family and in society.
17. Social rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring and developing the ability of a person experiencing social dysfunction to be able to carry out their social functions normally.
18. Repatriation is an effort to return victims of violence from the regional area to their area of origin.
19. Social reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, substitute family or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims.

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Region is the Nunukan Regency Region.
2. Regional Government is the Regional Government of Nunukan Regency. 3. Regent is the Regent of Nunukan.
4. Regional Work Unit, hereinafter abbreviated as SKPD, is an auxiliary element of the Regent and DPRD in the implementation of Government Affairs which are the authority of the Region.
5. Technical Regional Work Unit, hereinafter referred to as technical SKPD, is a Regional Work Unit whose scope of duties and responsibilities includes matters of Women's Empowerment and/or Child Protection.
6. Child is a person who is not yet 18 (eighteen) years old, including a child still in the womb.
7. Woman is a human being of female sex and a person recognized by law as a woman.
8. Women's Empowerment is every effort to improve physical, mental spiritual, social capabilities, knowledge, and skills so that women are ready to be utilized according to their respective capabilities.
9. Fulfillment of Children's Rights is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights to live, grow, develop and participate, optimally in accordance with human dignity and worth and receive protection from violence and discrimination.
10. Violence is any act that results in misery or suffering either physically, sexually, psychologically, and/or domestic neglect including threats to commit acts, coercion, or unlawful deprivation of a person's freedom.
11. Victim is a woman and/or child who experiences misery and/or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence that occurs in the Nunukan Regency area.
12. Protection is all actions of prevention, services and empowerment to protect and guarantee the rights of women and children from acts of violence.
13. Prevention is an activity carried out to prevent the occurrence of acts of violence against women and children. 14. Service is an action taken as soon as possible to victims when seeing, hearing and knowing that violence against victims will occur, is occurring or has occurred.
15. Empowerment is the strengthening of women victims of violence to be able to endeavor and work independently after they are recovered and provided with health and social rehabilitation services.
16. Health Rehabilitation is an effort to restore the condition of victims including physical, psychological and social health so that victims can carry out their roles properly and normally both in the family and in society.
17. Social rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring and developing the ability of a person experiencing social dysfunction to be able to carry out their social functions normally.
18. Repatriation is an effort to return victims of violence from the regional area to their area of origin.
19. Social reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, substitute family or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims.
20. Integrated Service Center, hereinafter abbreviated as PPT, is a unit that provides integrated services for victims of violence and is integrated with PPT that provides integrated services for witnesses and/or victims of human trafficking crimes.

Article 25

(1) The Regional Government is obliged to protect the fulfillment of the rights of child workers in the informal sector.

(2) Child Workers in the informal sector as referred to in paragraph (1) include: a domestic workers; b shoe shiners; c street vendors; d scavengers; e parking attendants; f children who work in agriculture, livestock and plantations; g children who work in mining; and h other informal sector work that employs children. (3) Every person who employs children in the informal sector must pay attention to the requirements: a minimum age of 15 (fifteen) years, except for the category of Worst Forms of Child Labor a minimum of 18 (eighteen) years; b obtain written approval from the parents/guardian of the child worker; c have a written work agreement between the employer and the parents/guardian of the child worker and obtain endorsement from the authorized agency; d not employed at night; e working time of a maximum of 3 (three) hours per day; f not employed in a place or environment that can disrupt the child's growth and development process, whether physical, mental, moral and intellectual or the child's health; g provide opportunities to obtain education in accordance with their talents and interests; h employ for light types of work; and i provide one day off per week.

11. Victim is a woman and/or child who experiences misery and/or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence that occurs in the Nunukan Regency area.
12. Protection is all actions of prevention, services and empowerment to protect and guarantee the rights of women and children from acts of violence.
13. Prevention is an activity carried out to prevent the occurrence of acts of violence against women and children. 14. Service is an action taken as soon as possible to victims when seeing, hearing and knowing that violence against victims will occur, is occurring or has occurred.
15. Empowerment is the strengthening of women victims of violence to be able to endeavor and work independently after they are recovered and provided with health and social rehabilitation services.
16. Health Rehabilitation is an effort to restore the condition of victims including physical, psychological and social health so that victims can carry out their roles properly and normally both in the family and in society.
17. Social rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring and developing the ability of a person experiencing social dysfunction to be able to carry out their social functions normally.
18. Repatriation is an effort to return victims of violence from the regional area to their area of origin.
19. Social reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, substitute family or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims.
20. Integrated Service Center, hereinafter abbreviated as PPT, is a unit that provides integrated services for victims of violence and is integrated with PPT that provides integrated services for witnesses and/or victims of human trafficking crimes.

7. Woman is a human being of female sex and a person recognized by law as a woman.
8. Women's Empowerment is every effort to improve physical, mental spiritual, social capabilities, knowledge, and skills so that women are ready to be utilized according to their respective capabilities.
9. Fulfillment of Children's Rights is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights to live, grow, develop and participate, optimally in accordance with human dignity and worth and receive protection from violence and discrimination.
10. Violence is any act that results in misery or suffering either physically, sexually, psychologically, and/or domestic neglect including threats to commit acts, coercion, or unlawful deprivation of a person's freedom.
11. Victim is a woman and/or child who experiences misery and/or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence that occurs in the Nunukan Regency area.
12. Protection is all actions of prevention, services and empowerment to protect and guarantee the rights of women and children from acts of violence.
13. Prevention is an activity carried out to prevent the occurrence of acts of violence against women and children. 14. Service is an action taken as soon as possible to victims when seeing, hearing and knowing that violence against victims will occur, is occurring or has occurred.
15. Empowerment is the strengthening of women victims of violence to be able to endeavor and work independently after they are recovered and provided with health and social rehabilitation services.
16. Health Rehabilitation is an effort to restore the condition of victims including physical, psychological and social health so that victims can carry out their roles properly and normally both in the family and in society.
17. Social rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring and developing the ability of a person experiencing social dysfunction to be able to carry out their social functions normally.
18. Repatriation is an effort to return victims of violence from the regional area to their area of origin.
19. Social reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, substitute family or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims.
20. Integrated Service Center, hereinafter abbreviated as PPT, is a unit that provides integrated services for victims of violence and is integrated with PPT that provides integrated services for witnesses and/or victims of human trafficking crimes.

Article 54

12. Protection is all actions of prevention, services and empowerment to protect and guarantee the rights of women and children from acts of violence.
13. Prevention is an activity carried out to prevent the occurrence of acts of violence against women and children. 14. Service is an action taken as soon as possible to victims when seeing, hearing and knowing that violence against victims will occur, is occurring or has occurred.
15. Empowerment is the strengthening of women victims of violence to be able to endeavor and work independently after they are recovered and provided with health and social rehabilitation services.
16. Health Rehabilitation is an effort to restore the condition of victims including physical, psychological and social health so that victims can carry out their roles properly and normally both in the family and in society.
17. Social rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring and developing the ability of a person experiencing social dysfunction to be able to carry out their social functions normally.
18. Repatriation is an effort to return victims of violence from the regional area to their area of origin.
19. Social reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, substitute family or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims.
20. Integrated Service Center, hereinafter abbreviated as PPT, is a unit that provides integrated services for victims of violence and is integrated with PPT that provides integrated services for witnesses and/or victims of human trafficking crimes.

Article 50

(1) To ensure synergy, balance and effectiveness of integrated measures in the implementation of policies, programs, activities, protection of Women and children, the Government conducts monitoring.

(5) Monitoring is carried out from planning to implementation of policies, programs and activities for the protection of women and children every year.

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Region is the Nunukan Regency Region.
2. Regional Government is the Regional Government of Nunukan Regency. 3. Regent is the Regent of Nunukan.

5. Technical Regional Work Unit, hereinafter referred to as technical SKPD, is a Regional Work Unit whose scope of duties and responsibilities includes matters of Women's Empowerment and/or Child Protection.
6. Child is a person who is not yet 18 (eighteen) years old, including a child still in the womb.

8. Women's Empowerment is every effort to improve physical, mental spiritual, social capabilities, knowledge, and skills so that women are ready to be utilized according to their respective capabilities.

18. Repatriation is an effort to return victims of violence from the regional area to their area of origin.

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Region is the Nunukan Regency Region.
2. Regional Government is the Regional Government of Nunukan Regency. 3. Regent is the Regent of Nunukan.
4. Regional Work Unit, hereinafter abbreviated as SKPD, is an auxiliary element of the Regent and DPRD in the implementation of Government Affairs which are the authority of the Region.
5. Technical Regional Work Unit, hereinafter referred to as technical SKPD, is a Regional Work Unit whose scope of duties and responsibilities includes matters of Women's Empowerment and/or Child Protection.
6. Child is a person who is not yet 18 (eighteen) years old, including a child still in the womb.
7. Woman is a human being of female sex and a person recognized by law as a woman.
8. Women's Empowerment is every effort to improve physical, mental spiritual, social capabilities, knowledge, and skills so that women are ready to be utilized according to their respective capabilities.
9. Fulfillment of Children's Rights is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights to live, grow, develop and participate, optimally in accordance with human dignity and worth and receive protection from violence and discrimination.
10. Violence is any act that results in misery or suffering either physically, sexually, psychologically, and/or domestic neglect including threats to commit acts, coercion, or unlawful deprivation of a person's freedom.
11. Victim is a woman and/or child who experiences misery and/or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence that occurs in the Nunukan Regency area.
12. Protection is all actions of prevention, services and empowerment to protect and guarantee the rights of women and children from acts of violence.
13. Prevention is an activity carried out to prevent the occurrence of acts of violence against women and children. 14. Service is an action taken as soon as possible to victims when seeing, hearing and knowing that violence against victims will occur, is occurring or has occurred.
15. Empowerment is the strengthening of women victims of violence to be able to endeavor and work independently after they are recovered and provided with health and social rehabilitation services.
16. Health Rehabilitation is an effort to restore the condition of victims including physical, psychological and social health so that victims can carry out their roles properly and normally both in the family and in society.
17. Social rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring and developing the ability of a person experiencing social dysfunction to be able to carry out their social functions normally.
18. Repatriation is an effort to return victims of violence from the regional area to their area of origin.
19. Social reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, substitute family or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims.
20. Integrated Service Center, hereinafter abbreviated as PPT, is a unit that provides integrated services for victims of violence and is integrated with PPT that provides integrated services for witnesses and/or victims of human trafficking crimes.

15. Empowerment is the strengthening of women victims of violence to be able to endeavor and work independently after they are recovered and provided with health and social rehabilitation services.
16. Health Rehabilitation is an effort to restore the condition of victims including physical, psychological and social health so that victims can carry out their roles properly and normally both in the family and in society.
17. Social rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring and developing the ability of a person experiencing social dysfunction to be able to carry out their social functions normally.
18. Repatriation is an effort to return victims of violence from the regional area to their area of origin.
19. Social reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, substitute family or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims.
20. Integrated Service Center, hereinafter abbreviated as PPT, is a unit that provides integrated services for victims of violence and is integrated with PPT that provides integrated services for witnesses and/or victims of human trafficking crimes.

Article 50

(1) To ensure synergy, balance and effectiveness of integrated measures in the implementation of policies, programs, activities, protection of Women and children, the Government conducts monitoring.

(2) Monitoring as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out by the Technical SKPD and PPT.

(3) Monitoring as referred to in paragraph (1) is to determine the progress and obstacles in the implementation of policies, programs and activities for the Protection of Women and children.

(4) Monitoring is carried out periodically through coordination and direct monitoring of SKPDs that implement policies, activities for the protection of Women and children victims of violence.

(5) Monitoring is carried out from planning to implementation of policies, programs and activities for the protection of women and children every year.

Article 54

(1) In the implementation of Protection of Women and children, the community can:

a. form family partners at the Kelurahan/Village level by the community;
b. conduct socialization of women's and children's rights independently; c. provide first aid to victims; and
d. report to the competent authorities if violence against victims occurs in their environment.
(2) Community participation as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out by individuals, community organizations, non-governmental organizations, educational institutions, religious institutions, private sector and/or mass media.

Article 51

(1) Evaluation of the implementation of policies, programs and activities for the Protection of Women and children victims of violence is carried out at the end of each Fiscal year or when needed as required.

(2) The results of the evaluation of the implementation of policies, programs and activities for the protection of Women and children victims of violence are used as input for the formulation of policies, programs and activities for the protection of Women and children victims of violence for the following year.

(3) Evaluation as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

Article 32

Exploitation as referred to in Article 27 letter e is caused by:

a. acts that exploit economically or sexually with the intention of benefiting oneself or others;
b. acts with or without the victim's consent including, among others, prostitution, forced labor or services, slavery or similar practices, oppression, extortion, exploitation of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully removing or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or exploiting the labor or ability of a person by another party to obtain material or immaterial benefits; and/or
c. any form of exploitation of sexual organs or other organs of the victim to obtain benefits, including but not limited to all activities of prostitution or obscenity.

Paragraph 1

Rights and Obligations of Women

Article 16

(1) Implementation of Fulfillment of Children's Rights in the field of health as referred to in Article 13 letter b, the Regional Government must provide facilities and organize comprehensive health services for children, so that every child obtains optimal health status from the womb, carried out gradually adjusted to regional financial capacity and supported by community participation.

(2) Comprehensive health services as referred to in paragraph (1) include: a promotional, preventive, curative and rehabilitative efforts for basic health services; b exemption from cost burden for malnourished children, children undergoing dialysis due to kidney failure, children with thalassemia major, children with disabilities, children with special needs, street children, children infected with HIV/AIDS, child workers, child victims of narcotics, alcohol, psychotropic and other addictive substances (NAPZA) abuse, children who become victims of violence, such as neglect, economically and sexually exploited and victims of human trafficking.

(3) Children as referred to in paragraph (2) are children from poor families except as otherwise regulated in accordance with health financing programs established by the government.

Article 53

(1) The Regent conducts guidance and supervision over the implementation of this regional regulation.

(2) Guidance and supervision as referred to in paragraph (1) include the provision of implementation instructions, guidance, supervision, monitoring and evaluation of the Implementation of Protection of Women and Children.

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Region is the Nunukan Regency Region.
2. Regional Government is the Regional Government of Nunukan Regency. 3. Regent is the Regent of Nunukan.
4. Regional Work Unit, hereinafter abbreviated as SKPD, is an auxiliary element of the Regent and DPRD in the implementation of Government Affairs which are the authority of the Region.
5. Technical Regional Work Unit, hereinafter referred to as technical SKPD, is a Regional Work Unit whose scope of duties and responsibilities includes matters of Women's Empowerment and/or Child Protection.
6. Child is a person who is not yet 18 (eighteen) years old, including a child still in the womb.
7. Woman is a human being of female sex and a person recognized by law as a woman.
8. Women's Empowerment is every effort to improve physical, mental spiritual, social capabilities, knowledge, and skills so that women are ready to be utilized according to their respective capabilities.
9. Fulfillment of Children's Rights is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights to live, grow, develop and participate, optimally in accordance with human dignity and worth and receive protection from violence and discrimination.
10. Violence is any act that results in misery or suffering either physically, sexually, psychologically, and/or domestic neglect including threats to commit acts, coercion, or unlawful deprivation of a person's freedom.
11. Victim is a woman and/or child who experiences misery and/or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence that occurs in the Nunukan Regency area.
12. Protection is all actions of prevention, services and empowerment to protect and guarantee the rights of women and children from acts of violence.
13. Prevention is an activity carried out to prevent the occurrence of acts of violence against women and children. 14. Service is an action taken as soon as possible to victims when seeing, hearing and knowing that violence against victims will occur, is occurring or has occurred.
15. Empowerment is the strengthening of women victims of violence to be able to endeavor and work independently after they are recovered and provided with health and social rehabilitation services.
16. Health Rehabilitation is an effort to restore the condition of victims including physical, psychological and social health so that victims can carry out their roles properly and normally both in the family and in society.
17. Social rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring and developing the ability of a person experiencing social dysfunction to be able to carry out their social functions normally.
18. Repatriation is an effort to return victims of violence from the regional area to their area of origin.
19. Social reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, substitute family or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims.
20. Integrated Service Center, hereinafter abbreviated as PPT, is a unit that provides integrated services for victims of violence and is integrated with PPT that provides integrated services for witnesses and/or victims of human trafficking crimes.
